podcast.title: Departure from Zero
podcast.body: Mark Wakefield was the original singer for the band Zero, featured on their 1997 demo EP. He left the band after facing numerous rejections, either due to discouragement or boredom, and subsequently became the manager for the band Taproot. "Part of the issue for zero's lack of success was, let's be honest, singer Mark Wakefield."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Singer for Zero
podcast.body: Mark Wakefield was the singer for the band Zero, the precursor to Linkin Park. He recorded the band's 1997 4-track cassette in his bedroom using a basic computer setup. "Everything was recorded in the bedroom of Singer Mark Wakefield using a root-of-entry computer setup."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Audition for Zero (1999)
xref.body: In March 1999, Chester was contacted by Jeff Blue to audition for Zero. He received two demo tapes—one with Mark Wakefield's original vocals and one instrumental—with the instruction to "Do your thing!" He wrote new lyrics, recorded his vocals, and sent them back, successfully passing the audition. "Chester wrote some new lyrics, recorded his vocals, and sent everything back. And that seal that he passed the audition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Audition for Zero
xref.body: Chester was contacted by a VP of A&R at Zomba Music and asked to audition for a promising band in LA called Zero, which needed a frontman. He received two tapes from Zero—one with existing vocals by Mark Wakefield and another with instrumentals. He recorded his vocal interpretations over the instrumental tape and sent it back, successfully securing the position. "Chester was asked to provide some vocal interpretations for the music, record them over the instrumentals and then send the tape back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Managed by Mark Wakefield
xref.body: Mark Wakefield, the original singer for Zero, left his band to become the manager for Taproot after Zero experienced numerous rejections from record labels. "Wakefield got the message or got bored or something and left to become the manager of a band called Taproot."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
